answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable stake that scales with the number of identities it controls, verified against a public atlas of prior work: every new identity must first complete a costly, time-bound proof task — like polishing an opal through a prism of independent checks — before it can transact. A Sybil attacker then pays the stake plus the compute cost per fake identity, so creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand times more than running one honest agent, while honest newcomers pay only once.
